newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine firms optimistic about 1997 - Price.
newsitem.headline: Argentine firms optimistic about 1997 - Price.

text.p: The vast majority of Argentine companies expect the economy and their businesses to be slightly stronger next year than in 1996, according to a poll conducted by the local unit of Price Waterhouse.
Eighty-five percent of those polled said they are moderately optimistic about the economy and two percent are strongly optimistic. Twelve percent were moderately pessimistic.
An even higher number, 95 percent, said they were optimistic about their own businesses with 77 percent moderately optimistic and 18 percent strongly optimistic.
The poll was conducted last month among 235 companies employing more than 200,000 people and with total revenues of $46 billion this year.

Sixty-one percent expect a slight increase in revenues while 17 percent expect the increase to be significant and only four percent think they will decline. Those forecasts were better than those a year ago.

As for prices, opinions don't vary much from those polled a year ago, Price Waterhouse said. Fifty-five percent think they will remain stable, 30 percent see them declining and 15 percent think there will be increases.

Regarding exports, 64 percent expect an increase, 29 percent see them holding at the same levels and seven percent think they will fall. These answers are slightly more optimistic than those of last year.

Price Waterhouse said the businessmen consider rigid labor laws, an unreliable judicial system, high unemployment (17 percent), high public spending and high taxes, in that order, as the main problems plaguing the Argentine economy.

It added that 44 percent of the companies believe they will not change their staff levels, 34 percent think they will cut jobs and 22 percent expect an increase in payrolls. This means a strong slowdown in the job reduction trend, Price Waterhouse said.
